# The Scottish Highlands

Green valleys, vibrant culture, towering mountains, historic castles and peaceful lochs: the Highlands is the Scotland of your imagination.

## The Highlands at a glance

- History & heritage:
Culloden Battlefield, Glen Shiel, castles, brochs

- Nature & outdoors:
Beinn Eighe Nature Reserve, Cairngorms National Park, Ben Nevis, Loch Ness, Loch Maree, Loch Shiel, Forsinard Flows Nature Reserve

- Wildlife:
Scottish wildcat, red deer, eagles, ospreys, otters, dolphins, seals, whales, puffins, ptarmigan

- Towns & villages:
Aviemore, Dornoch, Fort William, Gairloch, Glencoe, Inverness, Lochinver, Nairn, Portree, Thurso, Ullapool, Wick


Map of Scotland

## What to expect in the Highlands

Stretching across northern Scotland, the Scottish Highlands is home to rugged mountain ranges, deep glens, dramatic coastlines, and beautiful islands. Feel the community and warm Highland welcome as you learn more about the history, music and rich Gaelic culture of the area. This vast region offers a range of experiences, from scenic road trips to rare wildlife, castles and local traditions and events.

> "My heart's in the Highlands
>
> my heart is not here,
>
> My heart's in the Highlands
>
> a-chasing the deer."
>
> Robert Burns

## Highlights in the Highlands

The Highlands are a place of adventure, history, wildlife and spectacular scenery all year round. Home to iconic spots such as Loch Ness, Ben Nevis and Skye, this vast region also rewards those who journey to more quieter corners. Its experiences can easily fill weeks of exploration. These highlights offer just a glimpse of what the region has to offer.

### Experience the vast outdoors

From mountain adventures to coastal wildlife encounters, the Highlands offer endless opportunities to explore the outdoors. Walk through the dramatic landscapes of Glen Coe, take a boat trip on Loch Ness or head to lesser-known spots like Caithness or the Ardnamurchan Peninsula for remote trails, sandy beaches and breathtaking views. Follow long-distance trails such as the West Highland Way, Great Glen Way or the challenging Cape Wrath Trail. Explore the region by bike, take to the water with a range of activities or see the landscape from a different perspective at one of the region's ski resorts. Whether you are looking for a short trip or a longer holiday, the Highlands have got you covered.

[Discover the best walks in the Highlands](https://www.walkhighlands.co.uk/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2025/04/23/loch-beinn-a-mheadhoin)

Loch Beinn a Mheadhoin, Glen Affric

### Uncover the history of the Highlands

History and tradition are woven into the landscapes of the Scottish Highlands. Walk amongst iconic castles such as Eilean Donan, Urquhart and Dunrobin, explore the Glenelg brochs dating back to the Iron Age, and experience the unique Highland Games across the region. From Gaelic culture to old crofting traditions, there is nowhere better to connect with Scotland’s past.

[Experience the Highland Games in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/things-to-do/events/highland-games)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2025/06/27/eilean-donan-castle)

Eilean Donan Castle, Kyle of Lochalsh

© VisitScotland / Kenny Lam

### Wildlife spotting

The Highlands are one of the best places in Scotland to encounter Scottish wildlife. Watch thousands of puffins and other seabirds nest with boat trips from Wick in Caithness, spot the free-ranging reindeer herd in the Cairngorm Mountains, and look out for deer grazing the heather-covered hills across the region. Along the coast, spot dolphins playing in the water or take a boat trip from places like Plockton, Ullapool and Gairloch in search of seals and whales. If you're looking for adventure for the whole family, grab your binoculars and head to the Highland Wildlife Park for your chance to see wildcats, monkeys and Scotland's only polar bears!

[Learn more about Scottish wildlife](https://www.visitscotland.com/things-to-do/nature-outdoors/wildlife)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/11/11/cairngorm-reindeer-centre-in-aviemore)

Cairngorm Reindeer Centre

### Taste the very best local food and drink

Visit world-famous whisky distilleries and artisan coffee roasters to farm shops with fresh and local produce: the Highlands are a foodie paradise. Sample seafood along the coast, stop in local bakeries for fresh pastries or enjoy fine dining that celebrates the incredible flavours of the Highlands.

[Find your taste of the Highlands](https://highlandfoodanddrink.org/eating-out/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/10/08/20180228_mac_and_wild_falls_of_shin_mw_001.jpg)

Mac and Wild at the Falls of Shin, Sutherland

## What's on in the Highlands

From live music drifting through the glens to traditional Highland Games, you are sure to find some of the best events in the Highlands.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2025/07/18/belladrum-tartan-heart-festival.jpg)

### [Belladrum Tartan Heart Festival](https://tartanheartfestival.com/)

This popular music and arts festival offers a big Highland welcome with its mix of mainstream and emerging artists.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/07/13/pipe-band-marching-at-the-ballater-highland-games.jpg)

### [Highland games in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/things-to-do/events/highland-games)

Follow the sound of massed pipe bands, cheer on world-class athletes and join spectators celebrating one of Scotland's most iconic traditions.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/02/14/accordion-player-at-clachaig-inn-.jpg)

### [Blas Festival](https://www.blas.scot/)

Join a packed programme with live cèilidhs and concerts taking place across the Highlands.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/04/26/royal-dornoch)

### [Dornoch Music Festival](https://www.dornochbeerfestival.co.uk/tickets/)

Get ready for a weekend of fun for the whole family, with craft beers, delicious food and live music.

## See the Highlands through a new lens

In need of more inspiration for your next trip? Take a look at what our visitors to the Highlands have to say about this region. Explore historic castle ruins on the banks of a deep loch, walk through remote glens or taste the best local produce the Highlands has to offer.

## Discover your ideal location in the Highlands

From sandy beaches and rugged coastlines to towering mountain peaks, the Highlands offer an incredible variety of landscapes and experiences. Explore the regions below to learn what makes them unique.

### Caithness & Sutherland

Soar high above the golden sands of Ceannabeinne Beach on a thrilling zipline, hit the waves with North Coast Watersports near Durness or find a moment of tranquillity among the peatlands of the Flow Country, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. From beautiful beaches to impressive sea stacks and the northeastern tip of mainland UK, this area has some of the wildest scenery in the Highlands.

[Discover the stunning landscapes of the north](https://www.venture-north.co.uk/)

### Easter Ross

This peninsula north-east of Inverness is packed with hidden gems. Walk through Black Rock Gorge, which featured in _Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire_, or climb to the Fyrish Monument (seen on _The Traitors_) for spectacular views across the surrounding landscape. Meet the Mermaid of the North along the Seaboard Sculpture Trail and blow the cobwebs away on a refreshing stroll along the beach. Finish your day with a dram of Glenmorangie paired with some cheese from Highland Fine Cheeses.

[Escape to somewhere wonderful in Easter Ross](https://easterrosspeninsula.com/)

### West Highland Peninsulas

The most westerly point of the British mainland might be a remote corner of the Scottish Highlands, but it’s well worth a trip. Cycle through Ariundle Oakwoods in Strontian or hear the Singing Sands at Kentra Bay. Children will love searching for fossilised “Devil’s toenails” in Morvern, while clear nights offer the chance of some of the darkest skies in Scotland. It's the ideal place to switch off, reconnect and experience a quieter side of Scotland.

[Slow down in the West Highland Peninsulas](https://www.westhighlandpeninsulas.com/)

### Wester Ross

Touch three billion years of history with your fingertips in Wester Ross and see where two continents collided. Hike into the rugged mountains of Torridon or explore trails in Inverewe Gardens with its colourful display of flowers and plants. Pick up delicious homemade pies from Lochinver Larder for lunch before finishing the day with fresh seafood in one of the fishing villages along the coast.

[Step back in time in Wester Ross](https://www.visitwester-ross.com/)

### Getting to the Highlands

Driving

## Driving

Driving is the easiest way to explore the region to its fullest. The A9 links Inverness to southern Scotland. Both Glasgow and Edinburgh are around 3 hours away, while the west coast of Scotland is accessible via the A86 and A82 to Fort William. The A96 links Inverness to Aberdeen on the east coast.

Be prepared for single-track roads in some areas as well as busier traffic in the summer months.

[Read more about driving in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/driving)

* * *

Train

## Train

Inverness is a travel hub for the Highlands, with trains to and from places such as Nairn, Elgin, Kyle of Lochalsh, Thurso, Wick, or connections further afield to cities like Edinburgh, Glasgow and Aberdeen. There are train services to Oban, Fort William and Mallaig from Glasgow.

Find train times and ticket information with [Scotrail](http://www.scotrail.co.uk/).

* * *

Bus and coach

## Bus and coach

Long distance routes connect Inverness with other major cities, with local services providing onward travel in the region.

Check your route with [Stagecoach Bus](http://www.stagecoachbus.com/), [Citylink](https://www.citylink.co.uk/) and [Ember](https://www.ember.to/).

* * *

Flying

## Flying

Inverness Airport is located to the east of Inverness city centre, with a short journey time to the centre by car, train or bus. The airport has flights to and from destinations across Europe, including several airports in London.

It is also possible to fly to other airports in Scotland, including Edinburgh Airport and Glasgow Airport before travelling north to your destination.

[Discover more about flying to Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/plane)

* * *

## FAQs

When is the best time to visit the Highlands?

### When is the best time to visit the Highlands?

May to September is a great time to visit the Highlands, when the warmer weather creates ideal conditions for exploring mountains and lochs, though you can enjoy the Highlands all year round.

Spring (March–May): Take a wildlife cruise on the Moray Firth, where you may spot dolphins returning to Highland waters.

Summer (June–August): Spend a day on the beach among the mountains at Loch Morlich, enjoy boat trips on Loch Ness or hike some of Scotland's most iconic mountain trails.

Autumn (September–November): Admire spectacular autumn colours in Glen Affric, or head for a stargazing adventure in the Cairngorms Dark Sky Park.

Winter (December–February): Go up with the Nevis Range Mountain Gondola for a skiing lesson and enjoy spectacular views of the snow-dusted Highlands.

* * *

How long should I stay in the Highlands?

### How long should I stay in the Highlands?

You can experience some of the highlights in a particular area in 3 days but to really discover this vast region, you will need to spend at least 5 days (but ideally more!).

* * *

Where can I stay in the Highlands

### Where can I stay in the Highlands

The Scottish Highlands offer a wide range of accommodation options, from luxury hotels, self-catering stays, boutique guesthouses to welcoming B&Bs. Cities and towns have a larger range of places to stay than smaller villages or remote areas. Check out these handpicked locations for your next unforgettable holiday in the Highlands.

[Accommodation in Fort William](https://fortwilliam.co.uk/listing_cat/fort-william-accommodation/)

[Accommodation in and around Loch Ness](https://www.visitinvernesslochness.com/accommodation)

* * *

Can I explore the Highlands without a car?

### Can I explore the Highlands without a car?

Yes, but it requires some extra planning. Citylink and Ember have an extensive network of routes throughout the Highlands and run to major towns and villages. The train network is slightly limited in the northwest with local bus services being intermittent, so planning is essential.

[Plan your journey with Traveline](https://www.traveline.info/)

* * *

Can I explore the Highlands with my electric car?

### Can I explore the Highlands with my electric car?

Yes, there are charging stations dotted around the region, though there might be less in more remote areas.

[Browse charging points in the Scottish Highlands](https://chargemap.com/cities/highland-GB)
